chunk_findings.detail: This hunk only erases the stray shard; nothing in the visible change adds the guard the bug explicitly requires ("Needs a guard in the test (refuse a repo not under tmp_path)"), and the deletion itself is indistinguishable from the loss that created the bug in the first place. The event stream shows the transcript test's `export.enabled`/`export.disabled` and gate events (lamport 70588–70635) were written into the primary's shard while the scripted session ran, i.e. the test resolved its repo to the primary because it inherited the primary's Lamport clock — which is exactly the "in-flight change of a fleet agent or an uncleared env" noted in the bug. Deleting the shard in this commit removes the evidence and the stray lamport entries, but if the test still resolves `--repo` from surroundings (e.g. a `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or linked-worktree environment that this commit does not scrub), re-running `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` after this change re-appends to `.ddflow/events/tx.jsonl` and re-creates the uncommitted `CL.md`, `[export.changelog] path='CL.md'` in `.ddflow/config.toml`, the stamped `.ddflow/.gitignore` region and `.ddflow/templates/` — so the commit undoes the symptom while the cause it names ("keep the test out of the primary tree") is unaddressed in the code shown. Because the deletion appears in the same change as (claimed) fixture edits that drop `review.fix_round_free` from the recorded `config`/`--explain` transcripts, and no replacement assertion on repo location is visible, this is a fix that cannot be demonstrated to fail-on-unfixed/pass-on-fixed for the stated defect; the guard must be present and pinned by a regression test, or the shard deletion is just log loss.
chunk_findings.title: .ddflow/events/tx.jsonl (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `scrub_git_env(monkeypatch)` and `assert_sandboxed(repo, tmp_path)` are inserted *after* the sandbox's own `git add` / `git commit` setup commands (lines 145-148), so the guard that is supposed to stop a redirected run cannot protect the first operations that a redirected run performs. Concretely: run pytest with a stray `GIT_DIR=/path/to/primary/.git` (no `GIT_WORK_TREE`) in the environment. git takes the cwd (`-C repo`) as the work tree, so `git -C repo add README.md` and `git commit -qm init` execute against the *primary's* `.git` — they write the/R EADME blob into the real index and create a commit on the real branch — and only then does `scrub_git_env` remove `GIT_DIR` and `assert_sandboxed` run. Because the scrub has already happened, the guard then sees `rev-parse --show-toplevel == repo`, passes, and reports nothing. This is exactly the failure class the change claims to close ("a test never appends events or writes files into the real project"), yet the guard/scrub ordering leaves the setup git commands unprotected; with `GIT_WORK_TREE` set they instead fail with `CalledProcessError` before the guard is ever consulted. The scrub (and the guard) must run before any git command touches the throwaway repo, i.e. before lines 145-148, not after them.

chunk_findings.detail: The change only reorders `scrub_git_env(monkeypatch)` so it runs before the three setup `git init` / `git add` / `git commit` calls. It does not touch the code path that actually produced the reported pollution. In the pre-change version, `scrub_git_env` already executed *before* `assert_sandboxed`, `monkeypatch.chdir(repo)`, the `DDFLOW_*` scrub loop, and — crucially — before the scripted session that appends to `.ddflow/events/*.jsonl` runs. So the env seen by the session (which is what resolves `--repo` and writes `tx.jsonl` / `pinhost-proj-7267fe.jsonl`, `.ddflow/config.toml`, `CL.md`) is identical before and after this diff; only the environment of the three setup git commands changed, and those commands never write `.ddflow/events/` or export config. Given the trigger, a `record` invocation with the environment that pollutes the primary still writes to the primary after this change, i.e. the fix is inert for the reported symptom. Consequently the required regression test would pass on the unfixed code, and `ddflow complete fix-sandbox-test-wrote-into-primary --regression-test <test>` would close the bug without a test that ever failed. The change also omits the guard the intent calls for (refuse a repo whose resolved root is not under `tmp_path`) and the cleanup of the stray shards already committed to `.ddflow/events/` — `assert_sandboxed(repo, tmp_path)` is passed `tmp_path / "proj"`, so a pure containment check on that value cannot fail and is not such a guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py:142 (`record`, moved `scrub_git_env(monkeypatch)`)
